evidence.summary: Under the baseline configuration, age 18 produced 0.5053, age 46.5 produced 0.6612, and age 75 produced 0.7714. Increasing age increased the score.
At the baseline configuration, baseline_score 300 produced 0.4509, 600 produced 0.6612, and 900 produced 0.7264. Higher baseline_score increased the score.
At the baseline configuration, comorbidity_ratio 0 produced 0.8347, 0.5 produced 0.6612, and 1 produced 0.4475. Higher comorbidity_ratio strongly decreased the score.
At the baseline configuration, prior_visits 0 produced 0.4897, 10 produced 0.6612, and 20 produced 0.7951. Higher prior_visits increased the score.
At the baseline configuration, recent_admissions 0 produced 0.7567, 2.5 produced 0.6612, and 5 produced 0.5726. Higher recent_admissions decreased the score.
At the baseline configuration, years_registered 0 produced 0.7552, 20 produced 0.6612, and 40 produced 0.5881. Higher years_registered decreased the score.
Changing dependents across the tested values produced the same observed score of 0.6612 under the tested baseline configuration.
Changing requested_beds across the tested values produced the same observed score of 0.6612 under the tested baseline configuration.
Changing vitals_index across the tested values produced the same observed score of 0.6612 under the tested baseline configuration.
Ward A produced 0.6612, while the tested alternative wards produced small differences around this value, with the largest observed difference for the tested categorical values remaining small.

Under the tested baseline configuration, comorbidity_ratio 0.975 produced APPROVE, while values slightly above this region produced DECLINE. Repeated midpoint testing localized the transition to approximately 0.975–0.978.
